# Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS — facts

## Structure and components

- [statement] MDS-UPDRS assesses four domains: Part I non-motor experiences of daily living, Part II motor experiences of daily living, Part III motor examination, and Part IV motor complications; it is used in clinical care and research. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19025984/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS · also: https://www.movementdisorders.org/MDS/MDS-Rating-Scales/MDS-Unified-Parkinsons-Disease-Rating-Scale-MDS-UPDRS.htm
- [statement] The original MDS-UPDRS clinimetric study tested 877 patients at 39 sites and found internal consistency of 0.79–0.93 across parts; factor analyses supported separate part sum scores in preference to an all-parts total. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19025984/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] An independent Spanish-language validation in 435 patients reported intraclass correlation above 0.85 for each part total, while noting a moderate floor effect (30 %) for Part IV. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22865238/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] Part III examination instructions require recording medication status, time since the last levodopa dose, and clinical ON/OFF state; these conditions matter when interpreting repeated motor examinations. (medium confidence) — https://www.movementdisorders.org/MDS-Files1/PDFs/Rating-Scales/MDS-UPDRS_English_FINAL.pdf · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6851993/
- [statement] In a study of the MDS-UPDRS Motor Examination (Part III) with 728 paired investigations of 260 patients, minimal clinically important difference estimates were asymmetric: −3.25 points for minimal clinically pertinent improvement and +4.63 for worsening, using clinician global-impression anchors and distribution methods. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26578041/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] A 2017 study of paired investigations from 365 patients estimated minimal meaningful changes in Part I of more than 2.64 points improvement or 2.45 worsening, and Part II of 3.05 improvement or 2.51 deterioration; these are study estimates for the specified parts. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28218413/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] Original UPDRS and MDS-UPDRS scores should not be treated as interchangeable: a 2012 calibration study supported conversion formulas for Parts II and III, but did not achieve concordance for Parts I and IV. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22886777/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] The MDS Non-Motor Rating Scale (MDS-NMS) consists of 13 domains plus a subscale for non-motor fluctuations and is rater-administered; in its initial multicenter validation study, internal consistency was acceptable (average Cronbach's alpha 0.66 and 0.84 for the scale total and the non-motor fluctuations total), interrater reliability was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient >0.95) and test-retest intraclass correlation was 0.84 for the scale total. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31571279/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A 2019 PPMI analysis of 423 de novo patients estimated within-subject reliability of one-year change scores: Part II and Part III OFF each reached 0.50. Its authors cautioned that change scores contained substantial error variance. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6851993/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] Early-disease sensitivity requires caution: a Rasch analysis found floor effects and disordered response thresholds in Parts II and III; a separate comparison did not support greater sensitivity of MDS-UPDRS than UPDRS for mild motor severity in de novo PD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6647182/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS · also: https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mdc3.13329
- [statement] The MDS website describes the MDS-UPDRS as a revision of the original Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (developed in the 1980s) that addresses problematic areas of the original scale identified by an MDS review task force; it was developed to evaluate non-motor and motor experiences of daily living and motor complications, includes a motor evaluation, and can be used in clinical settings and in research. (low confidence) — https://www.movementdisorders.org/MDS/MDS-Rating-Scales/MDS-Unified-Parkinsons-Disease-Rating-Scale-MDS-UPDRS.htm · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] The PDQ-39 is a short 39-item quality-of-life questionnaire for Parkinson's disease whose data can be presented in profile form or as a single index; a briefer derived measure (PDQ-8) also exists. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9617716/ · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
